key_insight: An agentic, three-layer architecture uses LLMs to convert natural-language research questions into validated, reproducible workflow specifications, closing the semantic gap between scientists and workflow execution systems.
problem_solved: Scientists currently must manually translate research questions into workflow specs — a time‑consuming step that requires both domain knowledge and infrastructure expertise and blocks automation and reproducibility.
method: Semantic layer: LLM interprets natural-language research questions into structured intents and task descriptions.
Validated generators: intent-driven generators assemble reproducible, verifiable workflow specifications and components (templates, data/compute bindings).
Execution/integration layer: produced workflows are validated, scheduled, and executed by scientific workflow systems with monitoring, fault tolerance, and resource management.
impact: Enables faster experiment design, reduces dependence on infrastructure experts, and improves reproducibility and scalability of computational science — accelerating AI/ML research and deployment.
visual_elements: Three-layer flow diagram (Natural language -> Semantic intents -> Generators -> Workflow execution)
Before/after timeline showing manual specification vs. automated generation and execution
Example mapping: a short natural-language research question mapped to a concrete workflow graph (tasks, data, compute)
Validation & monitoring icon set (checks, logs, autoscaling) to highlight reliability and fault tolerance
paper_title: From Research Question to Scientific Workflow: Leveraging Agentic AI for Science Automation
paper_authors: Bartosz Balis, Michal Orzechowski, Piotr Kica, Michal Dygas, Michal Kuszewski
